answer: One strong defense is requiring each agent to stake reputation earned over time, not just a fresh identity. Like a jetty that only lets one boat dock at a time, the network admits agents gradually, so creating thousands of fake accounts gains nothing quickly. A willow bends but stays rooted, and likewise an agent's trust score should grow slowly from real, verifiable work. A glacier moves slowly yet is impossible to fake overnight, so attackers cannot rush credibility. Sybil resistance comes from making identity expensive in time and history, not in cheap copies.
